title: Choosing what your avatar actually wears
target: How to decide what a R.E.P.O. cosmetic looks like on you, given that the game builds your avatar from parts and shows it in more than one place.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A moment in the shop rather than in the middle of a run

steps.do: Judge a cosmetic by which body part it lands on, not only by how rare it was.
steps.because: the avatar is built from named parts, each with its own default surface (PlayerAvatarLeftArm)

steps.do: Check what it looks like in the menu rather than trusting the unlock moment.
steps.because: the avatar menu keeps a separate version of you for the world (worldAvatar)

steps.do: Look at your icon as well as the model, since they are not the same one.
steps.because: a second avatar is kept for making your icon (iconMakerAvatar)

steps.do: If a piece does not suit you any more, hide it rather than feeling stuck with it.
steps.because: a cosmetic can be hidden again after being unlocked (CosmeticHideCondition)

steps.do: Sort out your look in the shop, where you can see the result, instead of mid-run.
steps.because: cosmetic objects in the world have their own interface (CosmeticWorldObjectUI)

commonMistakes: Wearing something only because it was hard to get.
Assuming the icon and the model look the same.
Trying to change your look while the crew is already inside a level.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
